data.name: Pulut Adventure
data.detailed_description:
Pulut Adventure


Pulut Adventure is a 2D platform game with over 30 different stylistic levels and
exciting mechanics. Defeat the enemy and collect different of weapon to advance
your abilities. You can use the summon skills and flying mode to explore the world.

Game Features

  • Various types of monsters with unique behavior and gorgeous skills.
  • Defeat unique monsters to collect different weapon.
  • Each weapon has it unique skill.
  • Summon System.
  • Flying Mode.
  • Over 30+ levels with its unique mechanics.

Game Control

  • WASD or Arrow Keys to move the player.
  • J use sword
  • hold S D J to use sword skill
  • K to shoot
  • hold S D K to use shooting skill
  • F key switch to flying mode
  • L key to summon monsters.
  • Shift key to run.

reviews.review:
Pulut Adventure is an indie side-scrolling action game developed by yayapipi and published by Yayapipi Studio that embraces the spirit of old-school platformers while attempting to deliver a broader feature set than many games in its category. Released during a period when Steam was welcoming a wave of experimental independent projects, it stands as a title driven more by creativity than technical refinement. From the outset, the game introduces players to a colorful fantasy setting filled with monsters, collectibles, and an assortment of gameplay systems that extend beyond simply moving from one stage to another. Although its presentation immediately reveals its modest budget, there is an undeniable sense of ambition behind its design.

The adventure unfolds across more than thirty stages, giving players a respectable amount of content for a relatively small game. Progression is supported by a mixture of exploration and combat, with each level presenting new enemies and opportunities to acquire equipment. One of the title's more interesting features is its emphasis on collecting weapons from defeated foes. Rather than treating weapons as cosmetic upgrades, Pulut Adventure assigns unique abilities to many of them, encouraging players to experiment with different approaches. This creates a satisfying loop of discovery, particularly for completionists who enjoy uncovering every item hidden throughout a game world.

Beyond its weapon system, Pulut Adventure distinguishes itself with mechanics that are uncommon in indie platformers of its era. Players can summon creatures to assist them in battle, adding an extra layer to encounters that might otherwise feel simplistic. The inclusion of a flying ability also changes how levels are approached, opening alternative routes and giving traversal a greater sense of freedom. Combined with running, jumping, and skill-based attacks, these systems provide enough variety to prevent the experience from becoming repetitive. While none of these mechanics are especially deep on their own, their collective presence demonstrates a willingness to experiment that is admirable for a project of this scale.

Combat itself is functional and accessible. Enemies range from standard creatures to larger opponents equipped with flashier attacks, and the game attempts to keep players engaged through enemy variety rather than mechanical complexity. There are moments where battles can feel rough around the edges due to inconsistent responsiveness, but the overall pacing remains enjoyable for those willing to accept a few imperfections. The controls are straightforward and easy to learn, making the game approachable even for players with limited experience in the genre. However, veterans of precision platformers may occasionally find the movement and hit detection less polished than expected.

Visually, Pulut Adventure adopts a bright and cheerful style that complements its lighthearted tone. Character sprites and environments are simple, yet they carry a certain charm that reflects the passion behind the project. The soundtrack and sound effects are similarly modest, serving their purpose without becoming standout elements. Given the game's age, some aspects of its presentation understandably feel dated, but they contribute to the nostalgic atmosphere rather than detract from it entirely. Players who appreciate lesser-known indie releases may find its aesthetic reminiscent of the experimental titles that populated digital storefronts during the mid-2010s.

Like many small independent productions, Pulut Adventure is not free from flaws. Technical issues and occasional bugs have been recurring points of criticism among players over the years, and certain design decisions can feel unrefined. Some stages lack the balance and consistency found in larger platforming games, and there are moments where the game's ambition exceeds its execution. Nevertheless, these shortcomings are offset to some degree by the sheer number of ideas packed into the experience. It is a game that consistently tries to offer something new, even if every feature does not fully reach its potential.

Pulut Adventure ultimately succeeds as a charming curiosity within Steam's extensive library of indie titles. It may not redefine the platforming genre, nor does it possess the production quality necessary to compete with more prominent releases, but it offers enough creativity and content to justify a playthrough for fans of obscure adventures. Its blend of weapon collecting, summoning mechanics, flying exploration, and lengthy campaign gives it a unique identity that continues to make it memorable years after release.

Rating: 6/10
